title: Swallow's Nest
visualBrief: Small limestone seaside folly with a stepped rectangular hall, four low pinnacles, a round eastern tower with four tall crown spires, projecting balcony and wraparound terrace.

nativeAxes.front: +X tower above sea; -X entrance toward approach
nativeAxes.origin: Site anchor; Y0 standard PMTiles working datum.

identityFeatures: Three stepped masses ending in an eastern cylindrical tower
Four high crown spires and four lower hall pinnacles
Projecting circular balcony, crenellations and narrow perimeter terrace

reconstruction.basis: Inspected reference pictures and standard viewer PMTiles.
reconstruction.scope: Main exterior and terrace with bounded immediate rock apron reconstructed from pictures and coarse PMTiles; no complete cliff.

materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Two reference pictures and standard PMTiles define approximate current exterior fit; no bespoke survey sources.
Detailed original source geometry remains unchanged. An independent derivative adjusts vertical datum and bounded foundation skirts.
Stepped hall, round eastern tower, four tall crown spires, four low pinnacles, balcony and perimeter terrace provide identity. Openings, flags, balusters and floor heights remain simplified.

Coarse terrain cannot reconstruct the sheer rock face or exact balcony contact. A bounded immediate rock apron bridges the coarse PMTiles surface to the terrace; the sheer cliff face, long approach, vegetation and interiors are outside scope. No terrain cutout.
Four shared material graphs plus local opaque glass; no embedded texture images. Physical-device timing and continuous-motion shimmer remain pending.
importReason: Preserve eight spires, stepped massing and round sea tower in every level; closer tiers add pointed apertures, balcony rails and selected relief.
